Entries.SourceTerm: 清光照眼似迷家，明白轉身還墮位

Senses.PreferredTarget: Clear light fills the eyes yet seems to miss home; even a lucid turn still falls into position
SearchAliases: clear light fills the eyes yet seems to miss home; even a lucid turn still falls into position
Senses.Note: In a verse on the snow-lion case, Hongzhi says clear light can fill the eyes while one still misses home, and even a lucid turn can fall into a fixed position. Baiyu quotes the line after urging sustained practice, then warns that apparent arrival can fail at the next encounter. Zhe'an asks for a way beyond it and answers with a boat carrying moonlight. Linquan sets the couplet beside a moonlit river and presses the boat away from the shore. The warning tests subtle attachment to a successful view.

Senses.Explanation: Clear waves have no road through is literally a denial of passage through clear water. It first answers an unnamed monk’s question, ‘Is the buddha teaching like the moon in water?’ (佛法如水中月，是否). The records disagree over the respondent: Shitian Faxun raises the exchange under Jingqing Daofu’s name and criticizes how much talk he used, while Tianyin Yuanxiu raises it under Yunmen Wenyan’s name and classifies the three replies as all-enveloping, cutting off all streams, and following waves and currents. Gulin Qingmao reuses the line in an authored verse, pairing ‘outside the gate, clear waves have no road through’ (門外清波無透路) with ‘atop the peak, the blue well raises dust by itself’ (峯頭碧井自生塵). In the sole retained lamp recension, Huitang Zuxin asks how to discern the water channel and invokes old Yunmen within his own headword-bearing hall speech.

Lanshi, Yichu, Danya, and Liaozong each place it before a new verse that questions the usual map of nirvana and hell. Hengshan voices it at a funeral fire and asks where the deceased belongs if he fits neither named type. These are distinct current applications; the line itself should not be read as permission to break precepts.

Occurrences.Kwic: 浮雲散盡光皎潔，星自星兮辰自辰。讓和尚居南岳時，馬祖住傳法院，常日坐禪。師知是法器，往問曰：「大德坐禪圖什麼？」曰：「圖作佛。」師一日乃取磚於彼菴前磨，曰：「磨此何為？」師曰：「磨作鏡。」曰：「磨磚豈得成鏡？」師曰：「坐禪豈得成佛？」曰：「如何即是？」師曰：「如牛駕車，車若不行，打車即是？打牛即是？」於是悟旨於言下，遂印心傳法，符西祖讖「馬踏殺天下人」之語，南宗闡於江西。拈云：「坐禪求佛，捏目生花，磨磚成鏡，惑亂人心，這二老漢，正好一坑埋卻。」頌曰：南山下雨北山雷，馬師卻被讓師惑。一片浮雲消散盡，自知分明說向誰？頌雙林善慧大士，因梁武帝請講經，士陞座，以尺拊案一下，便下座。武帝愕然，誌公乃問：「陛下會麼？」云：「不會。」誌公云：「大士講經竟。」頌曰：大士講經太不良，卻於梁殿動龍顏。當時不得誌公老，走向雙林不得安。《法華經》云：「是法住法位，世間相常住。」頌曰：世間相常住，猢猻會上樹。芻狗吠天明，佳人不出戶。《文殊所說般若經》：「清淨行者不入涅槃，破戒比丘不入地獄。」頌曰：酒肆淫房隨處遊，十方世界任悠悠。閒來高隱千峰外，天不管兮地不收。《金剛般若經》：「應無所住而生其心。」頌曰：室居端坐默無言，夜靜更深月上窗。不覺西風連夜吼，無言童子口喃喃。《楞嚴經》云：「佛謂阿難：『若能轉物，即同如來。』」頌曰：若能轉物即如來，萬斧千刀劈不開。堪笑靈山會上客，瞿曇一坑都活埋。金陵誌公和尚令人傳語南嶽思大師云：「何不下山教化眾生，一向目視雲霄作麼？」思云：「三世諸佛被我一口吞盡，何處更有眾生可度？」頌曰：誰知更有眾生度，三世如來一口吞。路遠夜長休把火，大家吹滅暗中行。丹霞於慧林寺，遇天寒，取木佛燒火向，院主訶曰：「何得燒我木佛？」師以杖子撥灰曰：「吾燒取舍利。」曰：「木佛何有舍利？」「既無舍利，更取兩尊燒。」院主自眉鬚墮落。頌曰：古殿沉沉夜色深，欲將木佛劈為薪，只圖一夜烘烘煖，不管他人卻受驚。《法華經》：「此經開方便門、示真實相，深固幽遠，無人能到。」頌曰：深固幽遠隔千山，到者方知不夜天。萬語千言人不識，至今千古錯商量。昔有古德，一日不赴堂，侍者請赴堂，德曰：「我今日在莊上喫油餈飽也。」侍者曰：「和尚不曾出入。」德曰：「汝去問莊主。」者方出門，忽見莊主來謝和尚到莊。頌曰：近者不能聞，遠者不能見。世間

Senses.Explanation: Monastic regulations order the offices, movements, and shared conduct of the Chan community. Muchen Daomin defines them historically: early communities lived according to the code until Baizhang Huaihai established a monastery with a presiding abbot, two ranks of officers, and assigned duties. Zhongfeng Mingben likewise says Baizhang established the Chan community's regulations by drawing on the Vinaya code. Yulin Tongxiu uses the term as an enforceable boundary, warning against disordering it; his record's biographer separately reports a violation that scorned the regulations. Guxue Zhenzhe says the regulations restrain conduct and prevent the community's discipline from collapsing. Yichu Wuyuan states that an offender must be dealt with according to the old instructions. The term is therefore neither generic cleanliness nor decorum: it is the monastery's working rulebook, and the masters invoke it where authority is exercised.

Senses.Explanation: The breeze-and-moon scene that Chan rows set out as the realized life's own face and hand over as an answer. Feiyin Tongrong, at mid-autumn, grants the season neither cold nor hot, cool through the body, bright through all bounds — the clear breeze and bright moon ancient as ever, flowing water and high zither without pause, so everyone should know it without more chatter; Wuyi Yuanlai, over tea with the layman He, verses that school-gate matters few know and the great matter has its hour — today one thread runs through to you, and the breeze and moon fill the stream ahead; Pu'an Yinsu, tallying his mendicant freedom, counts a meal's fragrance, the breeze and moon, and chan-joy enough for a full lazy nothing, their drums aiding his workings while the midnight pine-song chants a tune; and Hongzhi Zhengjue, versing Zhang Zhuo's meeting with Changsha at the Yellow Crane Tower, rules that with hearts poured out and no one to heed, only the clear breeze and bright moon know. Ruibai Mingxue, asked what borrowing is in the five-rank drill, answers with four graphs — the clear breeze and bright moon — then verses the bodiless going and the descending hand past the front mountain; Hansong Zhicao, staking the seamless stupa and wordless stele on Wansong ridge, rules that to ask the cave mouth's deep meaning only the breeze and moon can answer; Jifei Ruyi, facing his donors' portrait, confesses joy is breeze and moon, anger running thunder and lightning — the wayfarer's liver and guts shown at once; and Tianyin Yuanxiu's staff leaps out on its own to say not hard, not easy — the breeze and moon share the note, heaven above or the human world below, wherever one goes.

Senses.Explanation: Xiang Yu is the historical figure used in compact Chan images. Cuiyan Shouzhi says that when a knowing listener inclines an ear, Xiang Yu crosses east of the river, then warns against taking the line too literally. Tian'an Sheng gives a closely shaped answer in a separate record. Dawei Xing uses Xiang Yu losing the horse Wuzhui as an image for failure to understand.
